paper_summary: Choqueuse et al. (IFREMER, 2010) describe test methods for hollow-glass-microsphere syntactic foams used as deep-sea pipeline thermal insulation: a buoyancy-based hydrostatic compression test giving bulk modulus and crush pressure, and Iosipescu / modified Arcan shear tests. An epoxy-matrix foam (Mat A) shows near-linear hydrostatic response with crush pressure ~90 MPa versus ~50 MPa for a polyurethane-matrix foam (Mat B) with the same microspheres; Mat A shear modulus ~800 MPa; Mat B is strongly rate-sensitive and cracks at ~120% shear strain. Temperature (4-100 C) strongly affects an epoxy foam (Mat C) but no numbers are given.

records.sample_label: Typical syntactic foam (Fig. 3, matrix not specified)

structure.microstructure_notes: Hollow glass microspheres 10-150 um diameter, wall thickness ~1.5 um, in polymer matrix; density < 1000 kg/m3.

test.specimen_notes: IFREMER buoyancy method: ~1 dm3 sample in hyperbaric tank, pressure ramp ~1 h; modulus_mpa = bulk modulus, strength_mpa = crush (collapse) pressure.

evidence.quote: The global behavior of the materials can be characterized by a first linear elastic response, where the bulk modulus of the material is identified (2.9 GPa), and the collapse pressure (95 MPa), called "crush pressure".

structure.microstructure_notes: Same grade of hollow glass microspheres as Mat B.

test.specimen_notes: Buoyancy-based hydrostatic test; apparent linear elastic behaviour up to 80% of crush pressure; strength_mpa = crush pressure. Initial bulk modulus stated as comparable to Mat B but value not given.

evidence.quote: the crush pressure of the material with rigid matrix is significantly higher than for the material with the soft matrix (90 MPa compared to 50 MPa)

structure.microstructure_notes: Same grade of hollow glass microspheres as Mat A.

test.specimen_notes: Buoyancy-based hydrostatic test; non-linear from start of test; strength_mpa = crush pressure.

evidence.quote: the crush pressure of the material with rigid matrix is significantly higher than for the material with the soft matrix (90 MPa compared to 50 MPa)

records.sample_label: Mat A (rigid epoxy matrix) - modified Arcan shear

test.specimen_notes: Modified Arcan fixture, 0.5 x 7.6 x 66 mm specimen bonded on aluminium supports; shear modulus comparable to Iosipescu result; sudden failure.

evidence.quote: The shear modulus obtained on material A (rigid matrix) is comparable (800 MPa) to the modulus obtained through the Iosipescu test whereas the results obtained on material B are significantly different.

records.sample_label: Mat B (soft PU matrix) - modified Arcan shear

test.specimen_notes: Modified Arcan fixture; strain_at_failure = shear strain at cracking initiation (~120%); strongly loading-rate sensitive (0.05-50 mm/min, Fig. 8, no values stated).

evidence.quote: It can be noted that the response of the material can be observed right up to cracking initiation, noted around 120% strain for material B.

extraction_notes: Text is heavily duplicated by the PDF extraction (each paragraph repeated many times); content is a 6-page conference paper with no data tables. Microsphere grade, volume fraction, densities and manufacturing route are not specified (paper only says foams are made by co-extrusion, lateral extrusion or moulding), so process_route='other' and particle details are null. Fig. 3 values (bulk modulus 2.9 GPa, crush pressure 95 MPa) are for an unnamed 'typical' material, matrix unspecified (matrix_class='other'). For hydrostatic records, modulus_mpa holds the bulk modulus and strength_mpa the crush pressure. Mat C epoxy temperature study (4, 50, 100 C) and Mat B loading-rate study are only plotted, no numbers given, so not recorded. Iosipescu shear curves (Fig. 5) and Arcan strengths (Fig. 7) not read from plots.
